name: Bookvara
tagline: Scheduling, payments, clients, and staff in one system for service businesses — the product is Vara.
description: Bookvara (Vara) is a management platform for shops that live on appointments: medspas, salons, wellness studios, and trades. I built across the interface and the backend so booking, the service catalog, client records, payments, and reporting stay on one set of data instead of three separate tools.

problem: A service business usually pays for one tool to take bookings, another to charge cards, and a notebook for client notes. Staff availability goes stale, two people get the same slot, and the owner cannot see the week without exporting something.
approach: One record for the appointment, the service, the client, and the payment. The calendar, the public booking flow, and the reports all read that record, so a change in staff hours shows up before the next person books.
solution: Vara gives the shop a calendar by staff, a catalog of services and products with price and duration, client history and notes, and checkout for cards and digital wallets. Clients pick a time online. Owners get a dashboard for revenue, appointments, and staff productivity. The same product is aimed at medspas, salons, wellness, and job-based services such as contractors.
features: Staff calendar with appointments, cancellations, and live availability
Online booking so clients choose a service, a time, and see the price
Service and product catalog with pricing, duration, and inventory
Client records: visit history, preferences, and notes
Card, debit, and digital-wallet payments inside the product
Dashboards for revenue, appointments, and staff productivity
Fit for appointment businesses and for job-based services
architecture: A multi-tenant web app. Appointments, clients, catalog items, and payments share one data model, so the calendar, the booking page, and the reports cannot drift apart.
